- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp downward move, model tends to underreact — correct by adding 0.5–1.0 to the forecast for the next 3–5 days.
- After a price spike (forecast > 70), model often overcorrects downward — adjust by +0.5 to +1.5 in the following 5–7 days to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.5) and forecast is flat or slightly rising, model tends to underestimate upward momentum — increase forecast by 0.3–0.8 for the next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon — apply a +0.5 to +1.2 offset to forecast for days 10–15 if sentiment is neutral or rising.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.5–0.8), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying correction.
- If forecast is below 65 and sentiment is rising, model often fails to anticipate upward breakout — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag in recognizing sentiment-driven reversals — if sentiment drops below 0.4, delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply +0.5 to +1.0 to avoid premature sell-off.
